destination.name: Port Stephens
destination.tagline: A bay and peninsula of white-sand beaches, big sand dunes and whale and dolphin cruises, north of Newcastle.
destination.description: Port Stephens is a bay and peninsula 30 minutes' drive from Newcastle Airport, with Nelson Bay as its hub and surf beaches at Anna Bay, One Mile and Fingal Bay. The Stockton Bight dunes cover 72 sq km and were used for scenes in Mad Max. Cruises leave Nelson Bay marina for resident dolphins from late November to May and humpback whales from May to November. Tomaree National Park covers the vegetated parts of the peninsula.
whyVisit: Climb Tomaree Head for harbour views

goodToKnow.title: Dunes get very hot
goodToKnow.detail: Wikivoyage says the dunes can reach 50C or more in summer, so winter, ideally after rain, is the better time for a sandboarding or 4WD tour.

goodToKnow.title: Lighthouse by boat
goodToKnow.detail: Point Stephens Lighthouse is visited by guided boat tour, about $120, and Wikivoyage calls a boat safer than walking across Fingal Spit; dates come from the operator.

goodToKnow.title: Getting there
goodToKnow.detail: Newcastle Airport is about a 30-minute drive, and the 130 bus from Newcastle runs roughly hourly, though a car is the best way around the peninsula.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}: dolphins are easiest to see from late November to May, and humpback whales pass from May to November.
